content: Original curator paraphrase of TradingView's public ATR-percent explanation: average true range percentage normalizes range-based volatility by the current closing price, computed as one hundred times ATR divided by close. True range incorporates gaps, unlike a simple high-minus-low range. The publisher's displayed ATR-percent example uses a fourteen-period Wilder relative moving average. This research supplement instead preserves the laboratory's existing fourteen-completed-true-range arithmetic mean, explicitly not the publisher's RMA. A maximum of 0.10 percent, equality admission, five-minute closed timing, trend-up/New York/normal-volatility context and use only as an additional entry veto are fixed laboratory hypotheses, not publisher-endorsed profitable settings. This new context was selected after earlier archive opportunity inspection; the reused archive is not untouched validation and no earlier outcome is reclassified.
